Customer to provide 2 weeks of anonymized traffic sample (logs) or synthetic workload profile
Schedule on-prem networking precheck with infra team (proposed Sept 2)

summary: CareAxis is scoping a 6-week POC to evaluate open-model inference for a multilingual EU healthcare assistant. Key goals: meet 95th percentile latency <250ms for short-turn prompts, multilingual quality parity for EN/DE/FR/ES, and data residency/SOC2 controls. They prefer Private (VPC) but open to Dedicated for initial run. Next: benchmark template, traffic sample, hosted quick demo, and network precheck.
topics: Workload sizing (concurrency, prompt lengths, peak RPS)
Quantization and batch sizing impact on cost/latency
Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted feasibility
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-14 16:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Anika (Redwood SE), Lena (CareAxis), Olivier (CTO), Sofia (Privacy), Marcel (DevOps), Priya (Clinical)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Lena (CareAxis): Hi all, Lena here — Director ML, joining from Berlin.
[00:11] Olivier: Olivier, CTO, hello.
[00:13] Sofia: Sofia, privacy and compliance.
[00:15] Marcel: Marcel, infra.
[00:17] Priya: Priya, clinical informatics.
[00:19] Maya: Great. Diego and I will take you through a quick scoping — goal is to map success criteria and pick candidate open models for a 6-week POC. Not a marketing deck, promise.
[00:30] Diego (Redwood): Quick context check: you said multilingual assistant for clinicians and patient-facing summaries? Can you confirm languages and percent traffic?
[00:38] Lena: Yes, core case is clinician summarization + triage assist. Languages: 55% German, 25% English, 12% French, 8% Spanish roughly. We also often get mixed-language utterances.
[00:50] Priya: Also need simple patient-facing discharge notes in plain language, in the same languages.
[00:56] Maya: Good. And regulatory constraints?
[00:59] Sofia: We're operating in Germany and France; data residency within EU is mandatory for patient PHI. SOC2 is required by procurement, but we also need clear KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. On-prem option would be ideal but VPC with strict routing is OK.
[01:15] Diego: That maps to Redwood Private or Dedicated. Private gives you full control; Dedicated could be faster to onboard but has different isolation properties. We'll sketch the differences in the benchmark template.
[01:25] Olivier: Cost sensitivity too — we have a constrained budget for the POC but we want a realistic performance run.
[01:31] Maya: Understood. Let's capture measurable success criteria first. What would make this POC a yes for you?
[01:38] Lena: Quality: for clinician summaries, we want precision on clinical facts — no hallucination. We plan to run an eval set of ~300 clinician notes across the four languages. Target: >90% factual accuracy on key fields (meds, allergies, diagnosis) as judged by clinicians.
[01:58] Priya: Usability: patient notes should be at CEFR B1 reading level in each language, and readability scores automated.
[02:06] Marcel: Performance: typical prompt length is 120 tokens, average output 250 tokens. Target P95 latency under 250ms for short-turn requests (we accept higher for long syntheses but want a baseline). Concurrently we expect 30 sustained qps with bursts to 120 qps for a few minutes.
[02:24] Diego: Helpful numbers. For modeling, can you confirm average tokens per minute and embeddings usage?
[02:31] Lena: Expect ~300k tokens/day initially. Embeddings used for retrieval: about 5k queries/day. But during peak hours, request rate spikes.
[02:39] Diego: OK — that gives us throughput targets. For the model shortlist, we recommend we test 3 model families across a few variants: Mistral medium-large, Falcon 40/180b variants (where available as open weights), and MPT-30B variants. Also consider Llama 2/3 derivatives where licensing allows. We'll also evaluate quantized versions (INT8/INT4) to reduce cost.
[03:02] Lena: We prefer permissive licenses — Llama variants may complicate enterprise use?
[03:06] Anika (Redwood): Right, license and commercial use considerations vary. We'll flag each candidate with license notes in the template. For EU health, we usually prioritize models with clear relicense terms or permissive community licenses.
[03:17] Olivier: On quality vs latency: we can accept slightly higher latency for improved clinical accuracy, but not beyond 500ms p95 for clinician-facing tasks. For patient-facing short texts, 300ms is okay.
[03:28] Diego: That tradeoff maps to model size and batching. Larger models give better accuracy but increase latency and cost. With Redwood features (KV cache, continuous batching, optimized kernels) we can often bring p95 down significantly for short-turns, especially with quantization.
[03:44] Sofia: What about on-prem? Our legal wants data never to leave customer VPC. How invasive is Private deployment?
[03:50] Maya: Redwood Private can run with a customer-controlled control plane and on-prem inference nodes; it integrates with KMS/HSM and produces audit logs. There's a setup window (usually 3-6 weeks) and an infra checklist — we'll run a network precheck during the POC prep. For the POC, some customers do hybrid: model weights in Private, control plane in EU. We'll document options.
[04:11] Marcel: We need to know egress and firewall requirements before committing.
[04:15] Diego: I'll add a network diagram and egress checklist in the follow-up.
[04:19] Lena: For the eval corpus: we can provide 300 gold notes but need guidance on anonymization — can Redwood accept synthetically generated data or must it be real?
[04:28] Maya: For initial hosted runs, synthetic or heavily anonymized data is fine. For private runs you can provide real sanitized logs. But we need the sample to mirror token lengths and language mix.
[04:39] Priya: Also want to test RAG — retrieval-augmented generation — for patient history lookup. How will that change the benchmark?
[04:46] Diego: RAG introduces embeddings cost and vector DB I/O; latency will include retrieval time. For POC we'll benchmark both pure-generation and RAG flows; we'll measure end-to-end latency and failure modes.
[04:56] Anika: We recommend doing two benchmark profiles: (A) Short-turn summaries (120/250 tokens) without external search; (B) RAG flow with 3-5 docs retrieved, test for tail latency. We'll include both in the template.
[05:10] Lena: Sounds good. Timeline? You said 6 weeks earlier. Can you walk through phases?
[05:14] Maya: Phase 0 (1 week): onboarding, dataset and network checks. Phase 1 (2 weeks): hosted baseline benchmarks across 3 model families and quantization configs. Phase 2 (2 weeks): Private/deployed benchmarks (if infra ready) plus RAG tests. Phase 3 (1 week): analysis, quality assessment with clinical reviews and decision meeting.
[05:33] Olivier: If infra isn't ready, can we still get meaningful hosted results?
[05:36] Diego: Yes — hosted runs let us measure quality and relative latency profiles. They won't capture VPC-specific network constraints, but they'll give you model selection guidance.
[05:43] Sofia: SOC2 and data residency — what artifacts do you provide?
[05:46] Maya: We'll send SOC2 attestation summary, data residency notes, and a KMS integration guide. For Private deployments we can arrange a security call with our compliance team.
[05:56] Marcel: For workload sizing, some more nuance: not all requests are equal. About 40% are short confirmations, 30% are summaries, 20% are discharge notes (longer), 10% are embeddings. We need the cost model per 1M tokens for each model/quant config.
[06:10] Diego: We'll include rough cost bands in the template and then refine after we run the hosted batch. Quantization (INT8/INT4) often halves cost but can change quality. We'll measure per-eval metrics so you can see the tradeoff.
[06:22] Lena: On multilingual quality: are there models that are particularly strong in German?
[06:26] Diego: Historically, some Falcon variants and Mistral finetunes do well for German, but you'll need evaluation. Llama-family models have good multilingual capacity in Llama3 line but licensing and weights availability may vary. We'll put candidate checkpoints: Mistral-7B/Chat variants, Falcon-40B (if available), MPT-30B multilingual, and a Llama-derivative where allowed.
[06:45] Priya: Could the POC include a small fine-tune on domain notes?
[06:48] Anika: We advise caution: for POC speed, prefer prompt-engineering and retrieval-first. A small LoRA fine-tune could be a Phase 2 experiment if hosted/private infra supports weight updates — that adds time and costs.
[06:58] Olivier: Any regulatory risk with fine-tuning on patient notes?
[07:01] Sofia: Yes, need explicit data handling and consent, plus HSM-bound keys. Fine-tuning with PHI is possible in Private but needs legal signoff.
[07:09] Maya: Noted. We'll flag that and isolate it as a separate deliverable if you want to pursue it.
[07:14] Diego: For benchmarks we'll provide scripts: load generator, evaluation harness (ROUGE/Factuality heuristics and clinician scoring), and latency collectors. We'll instrument p50/p95/p99 and token-per-second throughput.
[07:26] Lena: Can you show us a quick live demo of hosted latency with a Spanish prompt?
[07:29] Diego: Sure, we can run a short one now — quick heads-up the lines might have some noise in transcription if we record.
[07:33] [Live demo run: Diego executes a short hosted generation across two models — results summarized]
[07:45] Diego: Demo notes: Model A (Mistral-med-q8) p95 ~210ms for 120/250 profile; Model B (MPT-30B q4) p95 ~420ms; quality differences visible in handling medication lists. These are quick hosted numbers, we'll formalize in the template.
[07:58] Lena: Good to see. For the POC decision, who will be the approvers on our side?
[08:02] Olivier: CTO + Head of ML + Procurement + Privacy signoff. So likely Olivier, Lena, Sofia, and procurement rep.
[08:10] Maya: For Redwood, Diego/Anika will lead the technical work; I will coordinate commercial/contract and set up security calls.
[08:18] Priya: On evaluation: let's add clinician blind scoring and an automated hallucination detector — both in scope?
[08:23] Diego: Yes, we can integrate clinician scoring into Phase 3 and include automated checks. We'll provide the scoring sheet template.
[08:30] Marcel: Practical ops question: what's the deploy cadence for Private nodes? We have constrained change windows.
[08:35] Anika: Typically we provision a baseline infra and then push model bundles. For a POC we can schedule during low-change windows; provisioning takes a few days if network is ready.
[08:45] Sofia: We need a clear data flow diagram for legal.
[08:48] Maya: We'll attach a dataflow + KMS/HSM diagram in the follow-up.
[08:52] Diego: One more technical note: for multilingual mixed utterances we recommend byte-level tokenizers and testing sub-sentence code-switching. Some models lose coherence with code-switching, so include mixed-language tests in your evaluation set.
[09:05] Lena: We'll add samples.
[09:07] Maya: Quick recap of decisions and immediate next steps?
[09:10] Olivier: Run hosted baseline across the three families; provide cost bands and license notes.
[09:14] Lena: We'll anonymize and share 300 notes + mixed-language edge cases.
[09:18] Marcel: We'll schedule VPC/network precheck and confirm egress rules.
[09:22] Diego: Redwood runs the hosted benchmark and shares results and a recommended config for Private/Dedicated.
[09:27] Maya: Follow-ups: I'll email the benchmark template, SOC2 + compliance packet, and proposed calendar for the 6-week POC.
[09:33] Sofia: We'll want a security-only session before Phase 2.
[09:36] Maya: Noted — will set up a security deep-dive.
[09:40] [End recap and thanks]

Notes on transcript quality: automated captions had some mis-identified product names ("Redwood Dedcated" in a few lines), occasional overlaps. Shared artifacts referenced: "POC benchmark template (link)" and "Redwood Security packet (link)" — placeholders to be attached in follow-up.
